//: The cast and the rules governance.db is seeded from when it has no schema. Edit a row live in the database, not here — this file is read once, on first boot.

$LOAN and $APPROVALS are replaced at seed time with ARCADE_LOAN_TOOLKIT and ARCADE_APPROVALS_TOOLKIT. Tool names are PascalCase because arcade-mcp PascalCases them unconditionally (measured on #35); a rule keyed on get_loan matches nothing, and a rule that matches nothing is indistinguishable from a rule that permits.

$APPROVALS.Decide lists an argument the tool does not take: `approval`. It is not something a caller supplies — /pre resolves the request_id against approval_requests and writes the resolved facts into that key, discarding anything the caller put there. Catalogued because a rule condition may only read a catalogued argument, and optional because a request_id naming nothing must reach pre.decide-needs-a-known-request rather than be refused as a malformed call.
Emails are the fallback for a local run and must equal apps/idp/src/fixtures/people.json's. PERSONA_<KEY>_EMAIL overrides each one at seed time, exactly as apps/idp does.

Two output rules, on purpose (#16). post.redact-borrower-identifiers is act 3 and is conditioned on clearance — Riley and Morgan read the identifiers, Dana and Sam do not — because a control that redacts for everyone demonstrates nothing about identity. post.strip-injected-instructions is act 4 and is conditioned on nobody, because whether text is trying to give the model orders is not a question about anyone's authority; a chief credit officer must not be the one persona who reads the injection. Both fire on the same call and the audit row names each by id.

pattern.injected-instruction removes from the paste marker (or the tell itself, if there is no marker) to the end of the field. Proved against LN-2291 as apps/loan-app seeds it, byte for byte, in apps/hooks/test/post-redaction.test.ts, and proved not to fire on the other seeded notes. The previous regex here matched nothing — the note says 'Ignore any earlier instruction', not 'ignore previous instructions' — which is a rule that permits while looking like a rule that protects. Re-measure that test before rewording either the pattern or the note.

policy_rules.description: Act 1. A credit analyst never sees the approval tool: it is absent from tools/list, not merely refused.
policy_rules.reason: Credit analysts do not hold approval authority; the tool is hidden from this role.

policy_rules.description: Act 2. An approval above the caller's authority is blocked, and the denial tells the model how to escalate and then retry.
policy_rules.reason: DENIED: approving {{inputs.loan_id}} for {{inputs.amount}} exceeds your approval authority of {{subject.clearance}}. To proceed, call $APPROVALS.RequestApproval with action=approve_loan, resource_id={{inputs.loan_id}}, amount={{inputs.amount}} and justification=<why this loan should be approved>, then wait for the approval and retry $LOAN.ApproveLoan with loan_id={{inputs.loan_id}} and amount={{inputs.amount}} unchanged.

policy_rules.description: Act 2, the recursive turn. A decision on an id that names no approval request is refused before any other question is asked, so the answer says 'no such request' rather than tripping over a missing field.
policy_rules.reason: DENIED: no approval request matches that id, so there is nothing to decide. Do not retry; open the approval link again, or ask whoever raised the request to resend it.

policy_rules.description: Act 2, and PRD story 18. The person who asked cannot be the person who approves. This is what makes it safe to put the approval link in a conversation the requester can read: possession of the URL is not permission, and the check happens when the button is pressed.
policy_rules.reason: DENIED: {{subject.display_name}} raised this approval request, and separation of duties means the person who asks cannot also be the person who approves. Do not retry; it has already been routed to an approver whose authority covers it.

policy_rules.description: Act 2. Deciding is itself an exercise of authority: a clicker whose clearance does not cover the amount is refused exactly as the original call was.
policy_rules.reason: DENIED: this request is for more than your approval authority of {{subject.clearance}}, so deciding it is not yours to do. Do not retry; it has been routed to an approver whose clearance covers the amount.

policy_rules.description: A decision is final: once a request is approved or denied it cannot be decided again, so a denial cannot later be turned into an approval by clicking the same link.
policy_rules.reason: DENIED: this approval request has already been decided, and a decision is final. Do not retry; raise a new request if the outcome should change.

output_rules.description: Act 3. Masks the borrower's bank account number and tax id for anyone whose clearance is under 250000.
output_rules.reason: Borrower identifiers masked before the output reached the model.

output_rules.description: Act 4. Strips an instruction addressed to the model out of a loan file's free text, for everyone.
output_rules.reason: An instruction addressed to the model was found in free text and stripped before the output reached it.
